partner_context.their_ambition: The French Riviera is the densest luxury-coastal corridor in Europe — Saint-Tropez, Cannes, Antibes, Nice, Monaco — a continuous waterfront of marinas, superyachts, festivals and grand hotels where the sea is the natural way to move.
partner_context.their_pressure: The Basse Corniche and the A8 are gridlocked all summer; the 30 km from Nice airport to Monaco can take over an hour by road. Helicopter is the premium escape but it is loud, weather-limited and carbon-heavy — and the coast is tightening on emissions and noise.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: The Riviera's destinations are all on the water, minutes apart by sea. A foiling-electric tier turns the coast into a silent, fast, zero-emission waterway — the helicopter experience at a fraction of the cost and noise, gliding past the traffic.

hero.title: Navier × Côte d'Azur — the Riviera, by foil
hero.subtitle: Nice to Monaco in minutes, silent and over the water, while the Corniche sits in traffic.
hero.what_we_do_together: We bring a foiling-electric premium water tier to the French Riviera — linking Nice, Cannes, Antibes, Saint-Tropez and Monaco by sea. Navier supplies the software-defined fleet, captains and certification path; Riviera marina, hospitality and event partners bring the berths, the demand and the events calendar. Together we turn the most congested luxury coast in Europe into its fastest, quietest waterway.

why_now: The Riviera hosts the world's marquee events — the Cannes Film Festival, the Monaco Grand Prix, the Yacht Show — when road and helicopter capacity saturate completely. France and Monaco are both pushing hard on marine decarbonization and noise limits, and Monaco's Yacht Club and the region's marinas are actively courting electric propulsion. A foiling tier arrives exactly as the demand peaks and the diesel/helicopter alternatives come under pressure.
multimodal_fit: A foiling vessel meets guests at Nice Côte d'Azur airport's waterfront and the region's marinas, linking door-to-door with car and helicopter transfers. The water leg replaces the slowest, most congested segment — airport-to-Monaco, Cannes-to-Saint-Tropez — with a fast, scenic, silent run.

differentiation.why_navier: A foiling-electric premium tier — the speed and privacy of a helicopter without the noise, the emissions or the cost, and software-defined for a fleet that improves over time. Backed by an at-scale operating network in the Maldives.

proof_points.claim: The coast is built for the water.
proof_points.evidence: Continuous marina chain — Saint-Tropez, Cannes, Antibes, Nice, Monaco — all minutes apart by sea, hours apart by road in season.
France and Monaco are tightening marine emissions and noise rules; Monaco's Yacht Club actively promotes electric propulsion.

proof_points.claim: The events create acute peak demand.
proof_points.evidence: Cannes Film Festival, Monaco Grand Prix and the Monaco Yacht Show saturate road and helicopter capacity each year.
~100 vessels / $100M phased rollout already underway in the Maldives.

objections.concern: Is there demand beyond the summer season?
objections.response: The Riviera runs a near year-round affluent base — Monaco residents, business travel, shoulder-season tourism — and the marquee events create extreme peaks that road and helicopter simply cannot absorb.

objections.concern: How does it compare to helicopter?
objections.response: Foiling delivers comparable point-to-point time on the key coastal legs at a fraction of the cost, with near-silent operation and zero emissions — and it berths in the marina at the heart of each destination, not a remote helipad.

objections.concern: Noise and wake in sensitive ports?
objections.response: Foiling is near-silent and produces minimal wake at cruise — ideal for Monaco and the Lérins marine-protected waters where conventional craft face restrictions.
A clear first-of-class path, software-defined controls, and an operating record in the US and the Maldives to build the European certification case on.

phases.label: Phase 1 — the Nice–Monaco spine
phases.narrative: Launch the airport-to-Monaco corridor and the Nice–Cap Ferrat–Monaco coastal hop — the densest, most congested premium legs on the coast.
phases.rationale: Start where road congestion is worst and Monaco demand is strongest.

phases.label: Phase 2 — the full Riviera waterway
phases.narrative: Extend west to Cannes, Antibes and Saint-Tropez, adding the Gulf of Saint-Tropez crossing and event-surge shuttle capacity for Cannes and the Grand Prix.
phases.rationale: Connect the whole luxury-coastal corridor into one foiling waterway.

phases.label: Phase 3 — the Ligurian extension
phases.narrative: Add Quanta-LR reach across the Ligurian Sea — day-runs from Monaco and Nice to Corsica and the Italian Riviera — and run the coast year-round, not just in season.
phases.rationale: Extend the proven coastal waterway offshore: the hybrid opens Corsica and Portofino as same-day destinations and de-seasonalises the network.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet, captains, the maintenance and EU certification path, and the network playbook proven in the Maldives.
the_ask.partner_brings: Marina berths along the coast, hospitality and event relationships, and the local operating and concession framework.
the_ask.next_step: A pilot MOU on the Nice–Monaco corridor timed to a marquee event season.

close.title: The Riviera's fastest, quietest waterway.
close.body: The destinations are all on the water and minutes apart by sea. A foiling-electric tier glides past the Corniche traffic — the helicopter experience without the noise, the carbon or the cost.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the 'no charging at the islands' excuse. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.

end_state.headline: The French Riviera, re-platformed as a silent foiling waterway.
end_state.addressable_footprint: The continuous luxury-coastal corridor from Saint-Tropez through Cannes, Antibes and Nice to Monaco — plus the Îles de Lérins and superyacht anchorages.

steady_state.platform_mix: Pioneer II across the entire coast — every leg sits well inside the all-electric range
steady_state.tam_framing: Europe's densest concentration of marina berths, superyachts and luxury hotels, moving millions of premium coastal trips a year by road and helicopter.

end_state.narrative: Steady state is a silent foiling waterway spanning the entire Riviera — airport to Monaco, Cannes to Saint-Tropez, marina to yacht — the premium water tier of the world's most famous coast.
